what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted by roll call for the town to bring the sewer lateral to the Bright Farms property line, using the company's contractor.
A motion to approve the Bright Farms site plan from the sewer standpoint and pass it to the planning board was made; the vote outcome was not audible.
Members discussed metering Bright Farms' discharge; the business manager is to check with town counsel on billing by outflow metering, with the DPW director to follow up.
The commission voted to pay the final Woodard and Curran invoice, despite a dispute over extra consulting hours, and to assess privilege fees on 57 and 63 Crossroad.
It cancelled the 24 November and 29 December meetings and reviewed the FY21 sewer budget, which was running near a third of the year.

why_it_matters: The town, not Bright Farms, is paying to bring the sewer lateral to the property line, and members debated that cost because no betterment was paid, so it touches sewer rates and the sewer fund.
How Bright Farms' discharge is metered and billed will set what the company pays for sewer use compared with other users, and it is still unresolved.
The two Crossroad properties each face a privilege fee tied to the sewer project, and a town meeting article would move money into stabilization for a later betterment cost.
watch_next: The maintenance plan is to go on the agenda after next, once the new DPW director has reviewed it.
Counsel's answer on billing by outflow metering, and the planning board's handling of the Bright Farms site plan.
